channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Outsider em alta, Renan Santos anuncia um PM como seu vice na corrida ao Planalto
item.description: Businessman Renan Santos (Missão-SP) announced military police officer Aroldo Medina (Missão-RS) as his vice-presidential running mate for the 2026 election. The decision was made during a Missão party event in Rio Grande do Sul, where Medina presented Santos with a state bravery medal from his police career, symbolizing trust in the ticket. Both emphasized the gesture as a symbolic call to courage and electoral commitment.

item.title: 'Sinto que ela não quer', diz Valdemar sobre Michelle na campanha de Flávio
item.description: The national president of the PL, Valdemar da Costa Neto, stated that former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro is not showing willingness to participate in Flávio Bolsonaro’s 2026 presidential campaign. His remark suggests a possible lack of internal alignment in supporting the party’s candidate.

item.title: Câmara terá apenas duas semanas de votações presenciais durante campanha eleitoral
item.description: The Chamber of Deputies has decided to limit in-person deliberative sessions to just two weeks during the 2026 municipal election campaign, concentrating them between August 10 and 14 and one additional unspecified week. The measure aims to accommodate legislators' election campaign schedules, reducing the pace of plenary votes. The decision was made during a meeting of party leaders.

item.title: Crusoé: Um ranking dos melhores nomes para liderar a direita
item.description: A Bloomberg/Atlasintel poll shows that Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) is viewed by right-wing voters as the best candidate to lead the right and conservative agendas in the absence of Jair Bolsonaro. He was chosen by his father as the family’s presidential successor. The survey was released on Thursday, the 2nd.

item.title: Fotógrafo de Lula, Ricardo Stuckert deixará governo para integrar campanha à reeleição
item.description: Photographer Ricardo Stuckert, a close aide to President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva for 23 years, will leave the federal government to join Lula's 2026 re-election campaign. He will step down from his role as Secretary of Audiovisual Content Production and Dissemination on Friday, with effect retroactive to Saturday, and officially join the electoral team on Monday, where he will oversee social media coordination across X, Instagram, and TikTok in partnership with Nicole Briones.

item.title: Ibovespa avança com payroll fraco nos EUA e alívio para juros
item.description: The Ibovespa rose 1.40% on Thursday, driven by weaker-than-expected U.S. payroll data showing only 57,000 jobs added in June — far below the forecast of 110,000 — reducing pressure for a near-term Federal Reserve rate hike. The data boosted risk appetite in emerging markets and benefited Brazilian assets, particularly interest-rate-sensitive sectors like banking, with Bradesco (BBDC4) leading gains at +1.69%. Meanwhile, President Lula inaugurated the Major Sales Tunnel in Ceará as part of the São Francisco River transposition project, while investors monitor Middle East tensions and mixed movements in Brazil’s future interest rate curve.

item.title: Renan Santos escolhe tenente-coronel da reserva Aroldo Medina para vice na chapa do Missão
item.description: Renan Santos, 42, pre-candidate for President of Brazil, announced reserve lieutenant-colonel Aroldo Medina, 62, as his running mate for the 2026 election. The announcement was made on Wednesday night in Caxias do Sul, RS, during an event with supporters. Medina’s military background strengthens the ticket’s focus on security and experience under the Missão banner.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro diz a governo Trump que tarifaço daria 'vitória política' a Lula
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) sent a document to the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) warning that a proposed 25% tariff on Brazilian goods would represent a 'political victory' for President Lula’s government. He argues the measure would harm Brazil’s economy and strengthen Lula’s narrative of external aggression. The document was disclosed on February 7, 2026.

item.title: Governo Lula levanta informações sobre brasileiros sancionados pelos EUA por ligação com PCC
item.description: The Brazilian government is gathering information on Brazilians Victor Henrique de Oliveira Shimada and Stella Stefanie Nunes Henrique de Oliveira, sanctioned by the U.S. Treasury Department for suspected money laundering for the PCC. Brazilian authorities state that neither individual holds a central role in the faction, having only punctual involvement in specific transactions. The Lula administration aims to reinforce international cooperation against organized crime when possible, without initially contacting Ofac.

item.title: Bolsonaro deu ou não aval ao vídeo de Michelle contra Flávio?
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro claims that Jair Bolsonaro had prior knowledge of the video in which she attacked Flávio Bolsonaro, while Jair Bolsonaro himself denies having authorized or been aware of the recording. The conflicting accounts expose internal family and party tensions within the PL, with potential implications for political cohesion ahead of the 2026 elections.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula inaugura Túnel Major Sales no Rio Grande do Norte
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva inaugurates the Major Sales Tunnel, part of the Apodi Branch of the São Francisco River Integration Project, in Luís Gomes, RN, on Thursday, July 2, 2026. The 6.5 km tunnel, with a capacity to transport up to 20 m³ of water per second, will deliver water from the São Francisco diversion to western Rio Grande do Norte, benefiting 750,000 people across 54 municipalities in RN, PB, and CE. The project is seen as an advancement for water security in the semi-arid region.

item.title: TSE lança ferramenta para análise da participação do eleitorado brasileiro no exterior
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) launched the Overseas Voter Data Panel, a tool that consolidates historical microdata to analyze the participation of eligible Brazilian voters abroad. Developed in partnership between the TSE's Directorates of International and Strategic Affairs, the platform simplifies access to data previously scattered across complex spreadsheets and supports electoral logistics planning. The 2026 electoral register data will be released by the end of July.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro anunciará até amanhã o nome que concorrerá ao Senado pelo PL do Rio
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro will announce by the end of the day the PL’s Senate candidate for Rio de Janeiro, choosing between Senator Carlos Portinho and Deputy Carlos Jordy. The decision will be officially revealed this Friday at the PL’s 3rd National Communication Seminar in Rio. Portinho has the backing of the state party directory and mayors, while Jordy is favored by the Bolsonaro family and the hardline bolsonarist base.

item.title: Direita woke é o principal inimigo de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Senator Damares Alves, a prominent Bolsonaro ally, denounced in the Senate that she and her family are victims of criminal virtual attacks, including simulated extreme violence against her and her daughter. She described false images depicting her daughter being impaled and decapitated, and herself being decapitated. The speech reinforces narratives of persecution against Bolsonarist figures, positioning the 'woke right' as the main enemy of Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Eleições 2026: menos braço forte, mais mão amiga (por Felipe Sampaio)
item.description: The Brazilian Armed Forces show institutional maturity in 2026, with a serene climate in the pre-election campaign, contrasting with the tensions and coup risks of 2018 and 2022. The article emphasizes that the concept of 'friendly hand', inscribed in barracks nationwide, symbolizes the Armed Forces' commitment to the Constitution, democracy, and the rule of law, beyond humanitarian roles. Phrases like 'Ides Comandar, Aprendei a Obedecer' at AMAN reinforce discipline and hierarchy in war and constitutional respect in peace, indicating that the 2026 elections will proceed without undue military interference.

item.title: Jaques é recebido com vaias e placas "JaquesMaster" no 2 de Julho
item.description: Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) was booed during the July 2nd Independence celebration in Salvador, arriving alongside Governor Jerônimo Rodrigues while protesters displayed 'JaquesMaster' placards linking him to Banco Master, under PF investigation. The event, a key political stage in Bahia, was attended by no presidential candidates except Romeu Zema (Novo-MG), a pre-candidate for president. President Lula did not attend.

item.title: Caso Master divide percepção sobre aliados de Lula e Bolsonaro
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows 37.6% of respondents view Lula’s allies as most involved in the Banco Master financial fraud scheme, compared to 36% who blame Bolsonaro’s allies, indicating a near-even split in public perception. Conducted between June 26–30, 2026 with 4,999 respondents and a 1-point margin of error, the survey also found that the PF’s operation against Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) is widely perceived as damaging to Lula’s image and government.

item.title: Renan Santos, do Missão, anuncia Aroldo Medina como vice em chapa à Presidência
item.description: Renan Santos, pre-candidate for President from the Missão Party, announced Aroldo Medina as his running mate for vice-president during an event in Caxias do Sul (RS). Medina, a retired lieutenant-colonel of the Military Brigade, journalist, and former candidate in Rio Grande do Sul, accepted the invitation after presenting Renan with a medal. Both emphasized their partnership as a challenge and commitment to the Missão Party's political project.

item.title: Brasil responde a relatório dos EUA, nega que PIX favoreça empresas e defende decisões do STF
item.description: The Brazilian government formally responded to a U.S. investigation alleging trade barriers, denying that PIX or STF decisions favor companies or harm American trade. Chancellor Mauro Vieira stated the U.S. failed to prove discrimination or trade barriers, arguing the investigation targets Brazil’s sovereign policy choices, not unfair practices. Brazil highlighted its 2024 trade surplus with the U.S. and the favorability of its tariff structure to U.S. exports.

item.title: PF prende pastor Márcio Poncio na operação Unha e Carne
item.description: The Federal Police arrested Pastor Márcio Poncio during the 5th phase of Operation Unha e Carne in Rio de Janeiro, as part of an investigation into money laundering by a criminal organization linked to the illegal gambling game 'jogo do bicho'. The operation, authorized by Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes, also resulted in arrests of Adilson Oliveira Coutinho Filho (Adilsinho) and former state deputy Rodrigo Bacellar, with asset seizures up to R$22 million and 14 search warrants. The current phase stems from documents revealing parallel accounting, improper payments, and irregular electoral donations, suggesting ties between criminal groups and public officials, within the framework of ADPF 635.

item.title: Lula posa ao lado da suspeição
item.description: Lula, in campaign mode, maintains a constant performance of poses — from waking up to returning to bed — turning every gesture into political theater. His effort to distance himself from Jaques Wagner, implicated in the 'Master' scandal, lasted only a week, exposing the fragility of electoral staging. The text critiques the artificiality of candidates’ public performances during elections.

item.title: Atlas/Bloomberg: para 32,4%, casos como o de Wagner podem prejudicar muito candidatura de Lula
item.description: An Atlas/Bloomberg poll reveals that 32.4% of voters who have seen news about Senator Jaques Wagner’s (PT-BA) involvement in a public contract fraud scandal believe it could significantly harm Lula’s 2026 candidacy. The survey suggests the scandal is negatively affecting voter perception, particularly among those exposed to media coverage. This reflects electorate sensitivity to corruption allegations involving government allies.

item.title: Para 59%, caso Jaques Wagner afeta Lula ou parte do governo
item.description: An Atlas/Bloomberg poll from July 2026 shows that 59% of respondents aware of the Federal Police operation against Senator Jaques Wagner believe the case directly affects President Lula or part of the government. The Compliance Zero operation investigates financial fraud, corruption, and money laundering tied to Banco Master, leading Wagner to step down from his Senate leadership role, though he retains support from Lula, Jerônimo Rodrigues, and Davi Alcolumbre.

item.title: Atlas/Bloomberg: 37,8% acham que vídeo de Michelle enfraquece muito candidatura de Flávio
item.description: An Atlas/Bloomberg poll shows that 37.8% of voters believe the rift between former First Lady Michelle Bolsonaro and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro significantly weakens his presidential candidacy. Another 26.3% say it somewhat damages his chances. The findings highlight the perceived electoral cost of internal family divisions within the Bolsonaro clan.

item.title: Atlas: 37,6% ligam caso Master a aliados de Lula; e 36%, de Bolsonaro
item.description: The AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows 37.6% of Brazilians believe Lula’s allies are more involved in the Master case, technically tied with 36% blaming Bolsonaro’s allies. 17.1% see all political groups equally implicated, 6.1% point to the Centrão, and 3.1% are undecided. Additionally, 71.4% of voters closely followed investigations into Senator Jaques Wagner (PT) regarding the Banco Master scandal.

item.title: AtlasIntel: 37,8% acham que caso Jaques Wagner é um problema pessoal do senador
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows that 37.8% of respondents aware of the ninth phase of Operation Compliance Zero view the Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) case as a purely personal issue for the senator. Meanwhile, 35.6% believe it directly affects President Lula, and 23.5% see it as partially impacting the government. The results indicate a split in public opinion regarding the political significance of the Wagner case.

item.title: Atlas: 54,6% dos bolsonaristas não acreditam que Flávio foi grosseiro com Michelle
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll reveals that 54.6% of Jair Bolsonaro voters who watched Michelle Bolsonaro’s video do not believe her accusation that Flávio Bolsonaro was rude or disrespectful toward her, while only 29.9% believe it. Among Lula voters, 84.2% believe her claim. Overall, 59.6% of respondents believe Michelle’s account, with men (66.3%) more likely to believe her than women (53.3%).

item.title: Para 61,2%, investigação de Jaques Wagner prejudica candidatura de Lula
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll reveals that 61.2% of voters who followed the investigation into Senator Jaques Wagner (PT-BA) believe it could harm Lula’s re-election bid in 2026. The survey, conducted with 4,999 respondents from June 26–30, 2026, also shows 39.6% believe the case worsens the government’s image “a lot,” while only 4.4% think it improves it. The margin of error is 1 percentage point at a 95% confidence level.

item.title: AtlasIntel: 86,9% das mulheres bolsonaristas preferem Flávio a Michelle candidata
item.description: The AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows 86.9% of Bolsonarist women prefer Flávio Bolsonaro as the right-wing presidential candidate for 2026, versus just 10.8% for Michelle Bolsonaro. Among Bolsonarist men, 74.9% favor Flávio and 19.8% favor Michelle. Overall, 81.9% of Jair Bolsonaro’s voters back Flávio, highlighting a major rift in the Bolsonaro family and PL party after Michelle accused Flávio of humiliating her and dismissing her political role in a June 24 phone call.

item.title: No Rio de Janeiro, 1 em cada 3 eleitores não sabe em quem votar
item.description: In Rio de Janeiro, 36.6% of voters do not know whom to vote for president in the spontaneous poll, according to Paraná Pesquisas released on July 2, 2026. Lula (PT) leads with 28.2% of voting intentions, followed by Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) with 19.7%, while Jair Bolsonaro (PL), imprisoned and ineligible, was mentioned by 3.9%. The survey interviewed 1,600 people from June 29 to July 1, 2026, with a 2.5 percentage point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro empatam no Rio de Janeiro
item.description: Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro are technically tied in Rio de Janeiro for a potential runoff, with 44.7% and 44.4% respectively, within the 2.5 percentage point margin of error. The Paraná Pesquisas survey, conducted between June 29 and July 1, 2026, with 1,600 respondents, also shows a technical tie in the first round. The poll is registered with the TSE under number BR-BR-05371/202 and cost R$45,000.

item.title: Aprovação do governo Lula cresce e atinge 47,9% no RJ
item.description: In Rio de Janeiro, approval of President Lula’s government rose from 41.4% in April to 47.9% in July 2026, according to Paraná Pesquisas, while disapproval fell from 55.2% to 49.3%. Positive ratings (excellent or good) reached 33.8%, with a margin of error of ±2.5 percentage points and 95% confidence level.

item.title: A recuperação de Lula no Rio de Janeiro, segundo nova pesquisa
item.description: A new Paraná Pesquisas survey in Rio de Janeiro shows Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) now leads Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in both first and second round scenarios, with 41.6% and 44.7% respectively, though both remain within the 2.5-point margin of error. Despite the technical tie, the trend favors Lula, who lost the state in 2022 by about 1.2 million votes, while all alternative candidates remain below 2% in the first round.

item.title: Frase do dia
item.description: The article features a quote from journalist Cláudio Abramo stating that journalism is the daily exercise of intelligence and character, attributed via Agência Brasil. It also references updates from the Noblat blog, including a new Federal Police operation involving Sóstenes Cavalcante and claims of a 'war over spoils' accelerating the decline of the Bolsonaro family. No direct mention is made of 2026 election candidates.

item.title: Maioria acredita que caso Jaques Wagner pode atingir Lula e influenciar eleições, diz pesquisa
item.description: An AtlasIntel/Bloomberg poll shows that nearly six in ten Brazilians familiar with the Banco Master investigation involving Senator Jaques Wagner believe it affects President Lula or his government, with over 60% seeing potential impact on a possible re-election bid. Most (74.3%) think Wagner received undue advantages from the bank, and opinions on political responsibility are split among Lula’s allies (37.6%), Bolsonaro’s allies (36%), and both equally (17.1%). The case also damages the government’s image, particularly among Bolsonaro voters, 89.7% of whom say it significantly worsens their view of Lula’s administration.

item.title: Lula tem 41,6% e Flávio Bolsonaro 38,6% no Rio, diz Paraná Pesquisas
item.description: Lula (PT) reached 41.6% voting intention in Rio de Janeiro, up 4.9 points since April, and is technically tied with Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) at 38.6%. In a potential runoff, Lula leads with 44.7% versus Flávio's 44.4%, reversing the senator's previous lead. The survey interviewed 1,600 voters across 60 municipalities from June 29 to July 1, with a 95% confidence level and 2.5-point margin of error.

item.title: Atlas/Bloomberg: 32,4% acreditam que envolvimento de Jaques com Master pode prejudicar muito Lula
item.description: The Atlas/Bloomberg survey reveals that 32.4% of voters believe Senator Jaques Wagner's involvement in the Master Bank scandal could severely harm Lula's re-election bid, while 52.3% disapprove of the president. The poll also shows 74.3% think Wagner received undue advantages and 39.6% believe Operation Compliance Zero significantly damages Lula's government image.

item.title: Como trunfo eleitoral, Tarcísio inaugura linha de metrô 8 anos atrasada
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas inaugurated the first section of São Paulo’s Line 6-Orange subway, a project delayed by eight years from its original 2018 target. The state will spend an extra R$ 3.7 billion to complete the initial phase by October, aiming to leverage the delivery as an electoral advantage in his reelection bid. Tarcísio has politically exploited the completion of long-delayed, corruption-tainted infrastructure projects to criticize past administrations, including that of Geraldo Alckmin, who now opposes him indirectly through his support for Fernando Haddad.

item.title: Em 3 anos e meio, Lula deu menos da metade das entrevistas de Bolsonaro
item.description: In the first 3.5 years of his term, Lula granted 124 exclusive interviews, less than half of the 281 given by Bolsonaro during the same period of his presidency (2022). Bolsonaro exceeded Lula in every year analyzed, with the largest gap in 2021 (105 vs Lula’s 38 in 2025). In the first half of 2026, Lula gave 17 exclusive interviews across diverse outlets, while his ministers collectively granted 267—nearly 16 times more than the president.

item.title: CACB diz que teto do MEI proposto por Lula ficou abaixo da inflação
item.description: The CACB claims the Lula government's proposal to raise the MEI revenue cap from R$ 81,000 to R$ 110,000 in 2027 and R$ 140,000 in 2028 falls short of inflation accumulated since 2018 and fails to meet sector demands. The confederation advocates full inflation-adjusted updates, proposing caps of R$ 144,900 for MEI, R$ 869,400 for ME, and R$ 8.69 million for EPP, with automatic annual adjustments. CACB cites a PUC-RS study estimating the full correction could generate 650,000 new jobs and R$ 17 billion annually in new tax revenue.

item.title: Entre a efetividade silenciosa e o populismo irresponsável
item.description: Operation Hidden Flow revealed six fintechs operated as parallel banks for the PCC, moving over R$26 billion in four years, two days after Flávio Bolsonaro’s White House visit and the U.S. designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as foreign terrorist organizations. The article criticizes the symbolic use of the terrorism label, arguing these groups are economically motivated mafias, not ideologically driven terrorists, and warns that uncritically importing foreign security models erodes Brazilian legal principles and national sovereignty.

item.title: Verba do PL Mulher vai secar com saída de Michelle Bolsonaro? Veja o que diz Valdemar
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro's departure as head of PL Women sparked concerns about the future of funding for female party leaders, but Valdemar Costa Neto said the 2026 budget could be 'even higher,' anticipating more women elected. The PL Women initiative, aimed at boosting female political participation, received R$11 million in 2026 under her leadership. The shift follows a rift between Michelle and her stepson Flávio Bolsonaro.

item.title: Briga entre Michelle e Flávio abala plano bolsonarista para eleger Senado 'anti-STF'?
item.description: The public feud between Michelle Bolsonaro and Flávio Bolsonaro exposes internal divisions within Bolsonarism, threatening the strategy to unite forces for electing an 'anti-STF' Senate in 2026. Michelle accused Flávio of mistreatment during disputes over candidacies in Ceará, leading to her resignation from the PL Women’s presidency. The conflict reveals tensions over leadership and ideological alignment within the PL, as the right seeks to control the Senate to attempt the impeachment of Supreme Federal Court justices.

item.title: Na véspera da campanha, Lula reforça presença em redutos do Nordeste
item.description: Lula held events in Bahia, Rio Grande do Norte, and Ceará on the eve of the electoral blackout, inaugurating projects such as the Litoral Norte Hospital, the Major Sales tunnel, and the Salvador-Itaparica bridge, while delivering school buses and advancing the Transnordestina Railway and Novo PAC. These activities occurred before legal restrictions banning public works inaugurations from July 4, exactly three months before the October 4 election. The official campaign begins on August 16, following party conventions and candidate registration with the TSE.

item.title: Aliados avaliam que distância do bolsonarismo pode favorecer Caiado
item.description: PSD allies believe Ronaldo Caiado can stand out in the 2026 presidential race by distancing himself from Bolsonarism and building his own image. The announcement of Gilberto Kassab as running mate is seen as a move to strengthen the ticket, but polls show Caiado at 39% versus Lula’s 48% in a simulated runoff, trailing behind Flavio Bolsonaro. Despite low spontaneous support (2.9%), allies like Kassab and Goiás Governor Daniel Vilela insist Caiado is well-prepared and has growth potential during the campaign.

item.title: Além da vice, Flávio mira mulheres com plano para segurança e renda
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's (PL-RJ) pre-campaign is preparing the launch of the 'Brasil Por Elas' plan, targeting female voters with focus on public safety, income, employment, credit, and women's health. The plan is being coordinated by Daniella Marques (Republicanos), a potential vice-presidential candidate, with input from figures like Damares Alves. It will be unveiled on July 15 and incorporated into the government program for electoral registration by August 15.

item.title: Brasileiro apontando pelos EUA como ligado ao PCC teve relação com Corinthians
item.description: Brazilian businessman Victor Henrique de Oliveira Shimada was sanctioned by the U.S. for alleged ties to the PCC and money laundering via cryptocurrencies, including funds linked to the Corinthians-VaideBet sponsorship scheme. In Brazil, he was denounced by the São Paulo MP in 2025 for money laundering in the same case, where his company Victory Trading acted as a conduit for R$13 million. Brazilian investigations do not directly link him to the PCC but note connections with investigated firms and other São Paulo clubs.

item.title: STF entra de recesso, mas parte dos ministros segue de plantão
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) entered its judicial recess on July 1, 2026, with some ministers remaining on duty. President Edson Fachin will serve until July 16, followed by Vice-President Alexandre de Moraes until July 31. Ministers Moraes, Mendonça, Mendes, Dino and Nunes Marques will work full-time during the recess, while Zanin and Toffoli will handle specific case types. Fux, Carmen Lucia and Fachin (after July 16) will take vacations. In his end-of-semester review, Fachin highlighted approximately 60,000 decisions, over 11,000 of them collegial, underscoring the Court’s commitment to plural deliberation and institutional dialogue.

item.title: Michelle recebe apoio de aliadas 1 dia após deixar o PL Mulher
item.description: Michelle Bolsonaro stepped down from leading PL Mulher after three years, citing family priorities, but the timing coincided with tensions with Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, including disagreements over Ceará gubernatorial support and a video where she said she felt humiliated. A day later, she reposted messages from allies across multiple states praising her leadership and legacy.

item.title: Lula exibe curativo na cabeça após retirar câncer de pele
item.description: President Lula publicly displayed a bandage on his scalp following the removal of a basal cell carcinoma detected in April 2026, after undergoing 15 preventive radiotherapy sessions at the Sírio-Libanês Hospital in Brasília. He stated he showed the bandage to raise awareness about skin cancer prevention and mentioned delivering radiotherapy machines with Minister Padilha. The surgical procedure occurred on April 24, with radiotherapy completed by June 12, 2026.
